newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close year at record high.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close year at record high.

text.p: Caracas stocks rose in light trade to close the year at a record high with investors looking for further strong gains in 1997, traders said.
Venezuela made the biggest gains on the International Finance Corporation's (IFC) composite index of emerging market equities for 1996, showing gains of over 114.8 percent.

The market's leading index moved ahead 1.01 percent to close at 6,690.06 points despite a 73 basis points rise in six month TEM yields to 15.36 percent. Central Bank TEM bills are used as a benchmark for wider interest rates.
A total of 19.8 million shares traded worth 3.4 billion bolivars ($7.23 million).
Among traded issues, 25 rose, three fell and five closed flat.
Leading utility Electricidad de Caracas's share price opened at 478.30 bolivars after it was adjusted for a one for six share dividend. The stock closed up 75.00 bolivars at 483.00.
